requirements.requirement: Keep every installed curl package at its current version when normal yum system updates run.
requirements.summary: Both installed architectures remained at 7.15.5-17.el5_9. Yum directly parsed the persistent main-configuration exclusion as effective_yum_exclude=curl before and after reboot, and curl remained operational with clean RPM verification. Although repository failures prevented an update transaction test, the captured native yum configuration directly establishes the requested hold.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed CentOS release and kernel.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were observed before the change and remained identical after the completed reboot; the fixed lifecycle platform snapshot independently agrees.

requirements.requirement: Use an implementation compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The implementation used the platform's existing yum 3.2.22 configuration mechanism and installed no replacement package-management software. Yum successfully parsed the exclusion on CentOS 5.11.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Curl is persistently excluded by the legacy yum configuration and remained unchanged and healthy across reboot, while the OS release and kernel were preserved. The provider-wide restart protocol is coherent: pre-restart boot identity and task health were captured, restart was acknowledged, the node became unavailable during reboot, a different boot identity appeared afterward, and curl, yum configuration, SSH, runlevel, release, and kernel recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the identity transition.
limitations: No successful yum update or check-update transaction was captured because repository access failed with TLS/metadata errors; assurance of update behavior therefore rests on yum's direct parsing of exclude=curl rather than an observed update transaction.
The lifecycle package-health probe invokes an operation unsupported by this legacy yum and therefore does not independently establish general package-database health.
The restart evidence has no cluster-state probe, but the managed topology contains only one standalone node and no cluster service is identified.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated or reverted unnecessary mutation is established. The initial unprivileged write failed before either chained filesystem change occurred. The yum.conf backup and exclusion had clear safety and task roles, and the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. Two low-risk temporary artifacts nevertheless remained: /tmp/codex-reboot.log from the reboot action and /tmp/curl-rpm-verify.out from final verification; neither was cleaned. No package, platform, or exposure damage is shown.
